results.headline: Tatum's OT buzzer-beater sinks Brooklyn

sections.label: 1st quarter
sections.text: On the second night of a back-to-back, Boston fell behind early. Brooklyn won the quarter 31–26 and led for most of the first half.

sections.label: 2nd quarter
sections.text: The Celtics couldn't buy a three, going 2-of-16 from deep in the first half, and the winless Nets took a 61–56 lead into the break.

sections.label: 3rd quarter
sections.text: Boston's shooting finally came around: the Celtics hit eight threes in the quarter, two of them from Sam Hauser. They closed it on a 16–5 run, and Jayson Tatum hit the go-ahead three to send Boston into the fourth up 86–82.

sections.label: 4th quarter
sections.text: Paul George and Derrick White pushed the lead to 90–82 with 10:37 left, but Brooklyn got hot from deep and Julius Randle's basket made it 109–104 Nets with 2:57 to go. With the game tied, Tatum found White for an and-one dunk and a 114–111 lead with 33.7 seconds left. Boston led by four in the final seconds, but Randle made one of two free throws (117–114), Mitchell Robinson missed two at the line, and rookie Mikel Brown Jr. hit a corner three with 0.2 seconds left to tie it 117–117.

sections.label: Overtime
sections.text: Two Randle layups put Brooklyn back in front, and a Brown three made it 124–119 with 2:00 left. Randle fouled out with 1:02 to go, and George's free throws cut it to 124–123. Brown missed a layup with 2.3 seconds left, and out of a timeout Tatum took Brown off the switch and hit a 17-foot jumper from the left elbow at the buzzer.

performers.name: Jayson Tatum
performers.note: A season high, with 14 points in the fourth quarter and overtime, and the buzzer-beater to finish it.

performers.name: Paul George
performers.note: His overtime free throws cut Brooklyn's lead to one and set up the final possession.

performers.name: Derrick White
performers.note: His and-one dunk put Boston up 114–111 late, though he went 1-of-7 from three.

results.oppLine: Michael Porter Jr. had 27 points and 12 rebounds (6-of-12 from three); Julius Randle added 24 before fouling out in overtime, and Mikel Brown Jr. had 17.
results.takeaway: Three straight wins, but Boston shot 11-of-41 from three and Robinson went 1-of-4 at the line, nearly handing a winless team its first win.

results.headline: Kochetkov, Hurricanes end Bruins' point streak

sections.label: 1st period
sections.text: Boston struck on the power play 1:31 in: David Pastrnak fed Elias Lindholm from behind the net, and Lindholm found Pavel Zacha on the doorstep for a 1–0 lead. Tanner Jeannot fought Nicolas Deslauriers at 13:55. With 52 seconds left, Nikolaj Ehlers stripped the puck on the forecheck and Jackson Blake tied it 1–1.

sections.label: 2nd period
sections.text: No goals, but Carolina tilted the ice. Nikita Zadorov and Hampus Lindholm took tripping minors late in the period, and Boston went 20:39 without a shot from late in the second into the third.

sections.label: 3rd period
sections.text: The Bruins killed a 5-on-3 to open the period, and Matthew Poitras rang a backhand off the iron with an open net. At 10:19, Sebastian Aho finished a rush set up by Andrei Svechnikov and William Carrier for a 2–1 lead. Carolina then killed two Boston power plays in the final five minutes.

performers.name: Jeremy Swayman
performers.note: Kept Boston in it while Carolina outshot the Bruins 30–15, including six high-danger saves.

performers.name: Pavel Zacha
performers.note: His early power-play goal was Boston's only score.

performers.name: Elias Lindholm
performers.note: Set up Zacha's goal to stretch his point streak to three games.

results.oppLine: Sebastian Aho scored the winner, his eighth goal; Jackson Blake had the other, and Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 14 of 15 shots to improve to 8-0-0.
results.takeaway: The eight-game point streak is over, and it was Boston's first regulation loss since Oct. 5; 15 shots won't beat the East's best.

celtics.headline: Robinson's free throws nearly cost Boston
celtics.summary: Mitchell Robinson missed two free throws with 3 seconds left in regulation, opening the door for Mikel Brown Jr.'s tying three, and finished 1-of-4 from the line. Per AP, Robinson is a career 50.7% free-throw shooter and is 2-of-8 this season.

celtics.headline: Tatum clears first back-to-back since Achilles tear
celtics.summary: Tuesday was Jayson Tatum's first back-to-back since tearing his Achilles in May 2025, and he scored a season-high 40 with 18 made free throws, career highs in makes and attempts. Paul George: "We got the ball to the MVP, and he took us home."

celtics.headline: Tatum doesn't want to be 'the face' of Achilles tears
celtics.summary: Tatum said the attention on his comeback has become a burden and he doesn't want to be known as the face of Achilles injuries, while adding he's willing to help other players. Boston gets a few days off before hosting the Bulls on Friday in NBA Cup play.

bruins.headline: Sturm: 'Way too many turnovers'
bruins.summary: Marco Sturm said Carolina won on "small details, puck management" and that Boston had "way too many turnovers" in the 2-1 loss. The Bruins finish their two-game trip Thursday at St. Louis (5-6-1), coached by Jim Montgomery and featuring ex-Bruin Brandon Carlo.

bruins.headline: Jeannot hoped fight would 'fire the guys up'
bruins.summary: Tanner Jeannot fought Carolina's Nicolas Deslauriers in the first period: "It was a spirited fight between both of us, and hopefully it fired the guys up." Sturm said the fourth line created chances in the third period.

bruins.headline: James Hagens tied for NHL rookie scoring lead
bruins.summary: Hagens, 19, has nine points (four goals, five assists) in 12 games, tied for the league lead among rookies, despite third-line minutes and no top power-play role. He also leads all NHL forwards with 16 blocked shots.

patriots.headline: Vera-Tucker out at least four games; O-line help may be coming
patriots.summary: Mike Vrabel said left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring, IR) will miss at least four games but "I don't think it's for the season." Right guard Ben Brown (knee) may practice this week, and guard Greg Van Roten and safety Dell Pettus could return to practice from IR.

patriots.headline: Vrabel reportedly fined $250,000, unhappy it leaked
patriots.summary: The NFL reportedly fined Mike Vrabel $250,000 for conduct toward officials (Jets' Aaron Glenn and Eagles' Nick Sirianni were also fined), per Albert Breer; the fine is held in abeyance and could be waived with good behavior. It stems from Vrabel telling an official it was "a terrible effing call" during the win at Buffalo. Vrabel declined to discuss it Monday, calling the matter confidential.

patriots.headline: Pats (4-3) head to Miami after extra rest
patriots.summary: New England plays at the Dolphins (1-5) on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS, coming off extra rest after last Thursday's loss in Chicago. The Patriots are 3-10 at Hard Rock Stadium since 2013, and a win would move them to 3-0 in the AFC East.

redsox.headline: Baseball sciences director Besky leaves for Nationals
redsox.summary: David Besky, the Red Sox's director of baseball sciences, is leaving for Washington to be a uniformed pitching strategist, per reports from MassLive's Chris Cotillo and the Baltimore Banner. He's the first offseason hire for ex-Sox assistant GM Paul Toboni, now the Nationals' president of baseball operations.

redsox.headline: Cora: 'I got fired because we didn't pitch in April'
redsox.summary: On WEEI's "Baseball Isn't Boring" podcast, Alex Cora said he believes he was let go because the team didn't pitch in April; Boston was 10-17 when he was fired. He admitted he "probably acted immature" with posts after his dismissal.

redsox.headline: Phillies hire ex-Sox hitting coaches Fatse, Cronin
redsox.summary: The Phillies named Pete Fatse hitting coach and Joe Cronin assistant hitting coach. Both were fired by the Red Sox in April along with Cora; Fatse had been Boston's hitting coach since 2022.
